rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says no Qur'anic verse gathers good and evil more comprehensively; al-Suyuti cites its transmission in al-Mustadrak.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود ما في القرآن آية أجمع للخير والشر من هذه الآية أخرجه في المستدرك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says this verse gathers all good and evil: justice and beneficence cover obedience, while indecency, wrong, and aggression cover every sin.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قرأها يوما ثم وقف فقال إن الله جمع لكم الخير كله والشر كله في آية واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Shihab explains the Prophet's description of his speech as comprehensive: many matters from earlier books are gathered into one or two expressions.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي شهاب في معنى حديث الشيخين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to accept what is easy gathers noble character: lenience in rights and religious invitation, avoiding harm and forbidden sights, and patience, forbearance, and deliberation.
rows.anchor: لأن في أخذ العفو التساهل والتسامح في الحقوق واللين والرفق في الدعاء إلى الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah reaches the utmost expression of divine transcendence and, according to a treatise by Baha al-Din ibn Shaddad, refutes about forty sects.
rows.anchor: فإنه نهاية التنزيه وقد تضمنت الرد على نحو أربعين فرقة كما أفرد ذلك بالتصنيف بهاء الدين بن شداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two terms encompass all earthly provisions and benefits, including vegetation, crops, fruit, straw, wood, clothing, fire, and salt.
rows.anchor: دل بهاتين الكلمتين على جميع ما أخرجه من الأرض قوتا ومتاعا للأنام من العشب والشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase compresses all defects of worldly wine: headache, loss of reason, loss of money, and running out of the drink.
rows.anchor: جمع فيه جميع عيوب الخمر من الصداع وعدم العقل وذهاب المال ونفاد الشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flood verse compresses commands, prohibitions, reports, address, description, naming, destruction, preservation, salvation, ruin, and extensive narrative into a strikingly concise utterance.
rows.anchor: أمر فيها ونهى وأخبر ونادى ونعت وسمى وأهلك وأبقى وأسعد وأشقى وقص من الأنباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eloquence of the flood verse has been treated in a separate composition.
rows.anchor: وقد أفردت بلاغة هذه الآية بالتأليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is singular throughout the Qur'an because its plural form is cumbersome; the phrase about earths like the heavens expresses all the earths.
rows.anchor: ذكر الأرض فإنها مفردة ولم تجمع بخلاف السموات لثقل جمعها وهو أرضون ولهذا لما أريد ذكر جميع الأرضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural heavens is used when multiplicity is intended, while singular sky marks a direction; in the denial of unseen knowledge, the plural covers every inhabitant of every heaven.
rows.anchor: أي جميع سكانها على كثرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies knowledge of the unseen to every being located in any of the heavens, as well as to those on earth; only God knows it.
rows.anchor: إذ المراد نفي علم الغيب عن كل من هو في واحدة من السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses plural winds in contexts of mercy and singular wind in contexts of punishment.
rows.anchor: فحيث ذكرت في سياق الرحمة جمعت أو في سياق العذاب أفردت

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports that every Qur'anic plural form of winds denotes mercy and every singular form denotes punishment; Ibn Abi Hatim and others transmit the report.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال كل شيء في القرآن من الرياح فهو رحمة وكل شيء فيه من الريح فهو عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source cites a prophetic prayer asking for winds rather than a single wind, and explains that merciful winds vary and temper one another, whereas punitive wind arrives from one unopposed direction.
rows.anchor: ورد في الحديث اللهم اجعلها رياحا ولا تجعلها ريحا وذكر في حكمة ذلك أن رياح الرحمة مختلفة الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular wind in Jonah 10:22 is an exception: it linguistically parallels the contrasting storm wind, and one steady wind is needed for safe sailing; this is reinforced by its being called good.
rows.anchor: ومعنوي وهو أن تمام الرحمة هناك إنما تحصل بوحدة الريح لا باختلافها

rows.speaker: الأئمة الثلاثة
rows.claim: The three other major imams hold that the reward of Qur'an recitation can reach the deceased.
rows.anchor: الأئمة الثلاثة على وصول ثواب القراءة للميت ومذهبنا خلافه

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's school disagrees, citing the verse's statement that a person has only what they strove for as evidence against the reward of recitation reaching the dead.
rows.anchor: ومذهبنا خلافه لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted list of Medinan revelations begins with al-Baqara, Aal Imran, al-Anfal, al-Ahzab, al-Ma'ida, and al-Mumtahana, and continues through the final surah.
rows.anchor: وأنزل بالمدينة سورة البقرة ثم آل عمران ثم الأنفال ثم الأحزاب ثم المائدة ثم الممتحنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti calls the reported sequence strange and questionable, while noting that Jabir ibn Zayd was a leading scholar of the Qur'an and that al-Jaʿbari relied on the report for a revelation-order poem.
rows.anchor: قلت هذا سياق غريب وفي هذا الترتيب نظر وجابر بن زيد من علماء التابعين بالقرآن وقد اعتمد البرهان الجعبري

rows.speaker: البرهان الجعبري
rows.claim: Al-Jaʿbari's poem places al-Qamar among the Meccan revelations, after al-Tariq in its sequence.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتمد البرهان الجعبري على هذا الأثر في قصيدته

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa's report says the Prophet recited al-Baqara, Aal Imran, and al-Nisa in prayer.
rows.anchor: ما ثبت من قراءته صلى الله عليه وسلم لسور عديدة كسورة البقرة وآل عمران والنساء في حديث حذيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet recited al-Aʿraf in the Maghrib prayer, according to al-Bukhari.
rows.anchor: والأعراف في صحيح البخاري أنه قرأها في المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet recited al-Mu'minun in the dawn prayer and, on reaching Moses and Aaron, coughed and bowed, according to al-Nasa'i.
rows.anchor: روى النسائي أنه قرأها في الصبح حتى إذا جاء ذكر موسى وهارون أخذته سعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani reports that the Prophet recited al-Rum in the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: والروم روى الطبراني أنه قرأها في الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet regularly recited al-Sajda and al-Insan in the dawn prayer on Fridays, according to al-Bukhari and Muslim.
rows.anchor: روى الشيخان أنه كان يقرؤهما في صبح الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet recited Qaf in the sermon.
rows.anchor: في صحيح مسلم أنه كان يقرؤها في الخطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hakim and others report that the Prophet recited al-Rahman to the jinn.
rows.anchor: في المستدرك وغيره أنه قرأها على الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound report says the Prophet recited al-Najm in Mecca before the polytheists and prostrated at its end.
rows.anchor: في الصحيح قرأها بمكة على الكفار وسجد في آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet recited al-Qamar together with Qaf at the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: عند مسلم أنه كان يقرؤها مع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet recited al-Jumuʿa and al-Munafiqun in the Friday prayer.
rows.anchor: والجمعة والمنافقون في مسلم أنه كان يقرأ بهما في صلاة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hakim reports that the Prophet recited al-Saff to ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam when it was revealed, through to its end.
rows.anchor: والصف في المستدرك عن عبد الله بن سلام أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأها عليهم حين أنزلت حتى ختمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's recitation of many surahs before Companions shows that verse order within surahs was fixed by revelation; the Companions would not contradict his order, and Ibn Khuzayma says this reached mass transmission.
rows.anchor: تدل قراءته صلى الله عليه وسلم لها بمشهد من الصحابة أن ترتيب آياتها توقيفي

rows.speaker: الحارث بن خزيمة
rows.claim: A report complicating the fixed-order argument says al-Harith brought the two closing verses of al-Tawba, testified that he heard and memorized them from the Prophet, and ʿUmar confirmed him before they were appended to the Qur'an's final surah.
rows.anchor: من طريق محمد بن إسحاق عن يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه قال أتى الحارث ابن خزيمة بهاتين الآيتين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الكوفي
rows.claim: The transmitted order of Ubayy's codex places al-Qamar after al-Muddaththir and before al-Dukhan.
rows.anchor: ثم المزمل ثم المدثر ثم ﴿ اقتربت ﴾ ثم حم الدخان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat idha as extra in 84:1, reading it simply as the sky split, and compare this wording with al-Qamar's statement that the Hour drew near.
rows.anchor: قيل قد تأتي إذا زائدة وخرج عليه

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam lists indicators of permissibility, including permission, removal of blame, benefit, allowance, and silence about prohibition; praise alongside such a report indicates obligation or recommendation.
rows.anchor: وتستفاد الإباحة من لفظ الإحلال ونفي الجناح والحرج والإثم والمؤاخذة ومن الإذن فيه والعفو عنه

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: Some argue that the Qur'an is uncreated: scripture calls the human created in eighteen places but never calls the Qur'an created in fifty-four, and distinguishes teaching the Qur'an from creating humanity.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل جماعة على أن القرآن غير مخلوق بأن الله ذكر الإنسان في ثمانية عشر موضعا وقال إنه مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi, a leading Shafiʿi scholar, wrote a dedicated work on Qur'anic parables, which the Qur'an says are given for people to reflect on.
rows.anchor: أفرده بالتصنيف الإمام أبو الحسن الماوردي من كبار أصحابنا قال تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a prophetic saying that the Qur'an came in five forms: lawful, unlawful, clear, ambiguous, and parables; act on the lawful, avoid the unlawful, follow the clear, believe the ambiguous, and learn from parables.
rows.anchor: أخرج البيهقي عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi calls knowledge of parables one of the greatest Qur'anic sciences, but says people neglect it by attending to the examples while ignoring what they represent; an unrepresented parable is like an unbridled horse or unhaltered camel.
rows.anchor: قال الماوردي من أعظم علم القرآن علم أمثاله والناس في غفلة عنه لاشتغالهم بالأمثال وإغفالهم الممثلات

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts knowledge of parables that indicate obedience and warn against disobedience among the Qur'anic sciences a jurist must know.
rows.anchor: قد عده الشافعي مما يجب على المجتهد معرفته من علوم القرآن فقال ثم معرفة ما ضرب فيه من الأمثال

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam says parables serve remembrance and admonition; when they show degrees of reward, wasted deeds, praise, or blame, they indicate legal rulings.
rows.anchor: إنما ضرب الله الأمثال في القرآن تذكيرا ووعظا فما اشتمل منها على تفاوت في ثواب أو على إحباط عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parables exhort, deter, prompt reflection, reinforce, clarify meaning, and make abstract matters sensory and memorable by comparing the hidden to the clear and the absent to the witnessed; they also establish or refute claims and convey reward, punishment, praise, blame, and degrees of importance.
rows.anchor: ضرب الأمثال في القرآن يستفاد منه أمور كثيرة التذكير والوعظ والحث والزجر والاعتبار والتقرير

rows.speaker: الزركشي
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi says one wisdom of Qur'anic parables is teaching eloquence, a distinctive feature of this religious law.
rows.anchor: وقال الزركشي في البرهان ومن حكمته تعليم البيان وهو من خصائص هذه الشريعة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says analogy reveals meanings and brings conjectural ideas close to what is witnessed; the comparison should match the greatness or lowliness of what it represents.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري التمثيل إنما يصار إليه لكشف المعاني وإدناء المتوهم من الشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ten Companions were especially known for Qur'anic exegesis: the four caliphs, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr.
rows.anchor: اشتهر بالتفسير من الصحابة عشرة الخلفاء الأربعة وابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the caliphs, most tafsir reports come from ʿAli; reports from the other three are scarce, likely because they died earlier, and fewer than ten tafsir reports are known from Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: أما الخلفاء فأكثر من روي عنه منهم علي بن أبي طالب والرواية عن الثلاثة نزرة جدا وكأن السبب في ذلك تقدم وفاتهم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAli invited questions about the Qur'an and said he knew of every verse whether it was revealed by night or day, on a plain or a mountain; Abu al-Tufayl reports this sermon.
rows.anchor: قال شهدت عليا يخطب وهو يقول

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that the Qur'an came in seven readings, each with an outward and inward sense, and that ʿAli knew both.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم في الحلية عن ابن مسعود قال إن القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف ما منها حرف إلا وله ظهر وبطن

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAli swore that he knew the circumstances and place of revelation of every verse, saying God gave him an understanding heart and an inquisitive tongue.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال والله ما نزلت آية إلا وقد علمت فيم أنزلت وأين أنزلت إن ربي وهب لي قلبا عقولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti reports Ibn Masʿud saying he knew the audience and place of revelation for every verse and would travel to anyone who knew the Qur'an better than he did.
rows.anchor: ما نزلت آية من كتاب الله إلا وأنا أعلم فيمن نزلت وأين نزلت

rows.speaker: أبو البختري
rows.claim: Abu al-Bakhtari reports that ʿAli praised Ibn Masʿud as learned in the Qur'an and Sunna, saying that was sufficient knowledge.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم عن أبي البختري قال قالوا لعلي أخبرنا عن ابن مسعود قال علم القرآن والسنة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas was known as the Qur'an's interpreter, and the Prophet prayed for his understanding of religion, knowledge of interpretation and wisdom; Ibn ʿUmar reports another prayer for blessing and spreading his influence.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم في الحلية عن ابن عمر قال دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preceding example, the distant sense of wasat, the best or most upright community, is intended; the witness-bearing phrase reinforces it as a quality of the just, unlike the earlier unreinforced example.
rows.anchor: قلت وهي مرشحة بلازم المورى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word najm can mean a star, suggested by the mention of sun and moon, or the more remote intended sense of stemless plants; this is a Qur'anic double entendre.
rows.anchor: فإن النجم يطلق على الكوكب ويرشحه له ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an instance of combining multiple things under one judgment: the sun and moon follow a reckoning, while the star or plant and tree prostrate.
rows.anchor: جمع المال والبنون في الزينة

rows.speaker: الزركشي
rows.claim: Different descriptions of Adam's creation refer to successive states, not contradiction: dust develops through altered mud and clinging clay to pottery-like dried clay.
rows.anchor: قال الزركشي في البرهان للإختلاف أسباب

rows.speaker: الزركشي
rows.claim: Moses' staff is called a great serpent for its form, but likened to a small snake for its rapid, light movement.
rows.anchor: قال الزركشي في البرهان للإختلاف أسباب

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Halimi reconciles verses that affirm and deny questioning by assigning the first questions to belief in God's oneness and the messengers, and the second to religious laws and their details.
rows.anchor: قال الحليمي فتحمل الآية الأولى على السؤال عن التوحيد وتصديق الرسل والثانية على ما يستلزمه الإقرار بالنبوات

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Resurrection has many stations: people are questioned at some and not at others.
rows.anchor: وحمله غيره على اختلاف الأماكن لأن في القيامة مواقف كثيرة ففي موضع يسألون وفي آخر لا يسألون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation distinguishes questioning for reproach, which occurs, from questioning to seek an excuse or establish proof, which does not.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن السؤال المثبت سؤال تبكيت وتوبيخ والمنفى سؤال المعذرة وبيان الحجة

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو الحسن الشاذلي
rows.claim: Al-Shadhili reads the command to fear God as fully due as a command about monotheism, supported by the following words about dying as Muslims, and reads the other command as concerning deeds.
rows.anchor: حمل الشيخ أبو الحسن الشاذلي الآية الأولى على التوحيد بدليل قوله بعدها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the command to fear God as fully due was abrogated by the command to fear Him as far as one is able.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل الثانية ناسخة للأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conflict about justice between wives is resolved by distinguishing fair fulfillment of rights, which is possible, from emotional inclination, which people cannot control.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن الأولى في توفية الحقوق والثانية في الميل القلبي وليس في قدرة الإنسان

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali and others count five hundred Qur'anic legal verses, while some count only 150; they may mean explicit rulings, since stories and parables also yield legal inferences.
rows.anchor: قال الغزالي وغيره آيات الأحكام خمسمائة آية وقال بعضهم مائة وخمسون قيل ولعل مرادهم المصرح به

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam says most Qur'anic verses contain rulings through manners and ethics; rulings may be explicit or inferred, sometimes from one verse and sometimes by combining verses, such as a six-month minimum pregnancy.
rows.anchor: معظم آي القرآن لا يخلوا عن أحكام مشتملة على آداب حسنة وأخلاق جميلة ثم من الآيات ما صرح فيه بالأحكام

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam says rulings are indicated by legal wording, statements of permission or prohibition, or promised worldly and otherworldly benefits and harms; praise, love, acceptance, guidance, reward, forgiveness, safety, nearness, light, healing, and similar signs show a deed is either obligatory or recommended.
rows.anchor: ويستدل على الأحكام تارة بالصيغة وهو ظاهر وتارة بالإخبار مثل

rows.speaker: الزركشي
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi says an exegete must know Arabic vocabulary and grammar to uncover meaning: particles are treated in grammar books, while nouns and verbs are taken from lexicons, including the listed major dictionaries and verb glossaries.
rows.anchor: ويحتاج الكاشف عن ذلك إلى معرفة علم اللغة أسماء وأفعالا وحروفا فالحروف لقلتها تكلم النحاة على معانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti prioritizes sound reports from Ibn ʿAbbas and his students for rare Qur'anic words, especially Ibn Abi Talha's route, which al-Bukhari used and arranged by surah.
rows.anchor: وأولى ما يرجع إليه في ذلك ما ثبت عن ابن عباس وأصحابه الآخذين عنه فإنه ورد عنهم ما يستوعب تفسير غريب القرآن

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses idha in 17:18 as governed in the genitive by hatta.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش في قوله تعالى ﴿ حتى إذا جاؤوها ﴾ إن إذا جر بحتى

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: For accusative readings of khafida and rafiʿa, Ibn Jinni makes the first idha a subject and the second its predicate, with the accusative descriptions as circumstantial clauses; the event lowers some and raises others.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جني في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا وقعت الواقعة ﴾ الآية

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most grammarians reject taking idha outside its adverbial role: hatta begins the full clause, the second idha apposes the first, and the first has an omitted response inferred as the people dividing into three groups.
rows.anchor: والجمهور أنكروا خروجها عن الظرفية وقالوا في الآية الأولى إن حتى حرف ابتداء داخل على الجملة بأسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idha can refer to the present rather than the future when the described action occurs alongside the named time, as with night, day, and the setting star.
rows.anchor: فترد للحال نحو ﴿ والليل إذا يغشى ﴾ فإن الغشيان مقارن لليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idha can also refer to the past in reports revealed after the events, such as people seeing trade, Dhu al-Qarnayn reaching the sunrise, or building the barrier.
rows.anchor: نحو ﴿ وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا ﴾ الآية فإن الآية نزلت بعد الرؤية والانفضاض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In some verses idha is temporal rather than conditional: if it were conditional, a nominal-clause response would require fa; proposed ellipses and alternative parses are rejected as forced or unnecessary.
rows.anchor: نحو ﴿ وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون ﴾ ﴿ والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an adjective follows a construct phrase whose first element is a number, it may agree with either the construct head or its complement, as shown by seven heavens in tiers and seven fat cows.
rows.anchor: فمن الأول ﴿ سبع سماوات طباقا ﴾ ومن الثاني ﴿ سبع بقرات سمان ﴾
